about.title: About CD Calculator - Certificate of Deposit Investment Tool
about.description: The CD Calculator is a comprehensive savings tool designed to help you calculate returns on Certificate of Deposit investments and compare CD rates from different banks. Whether you're evaluating short-term or long-term CDs, this calculator provides accurate projections for interest earnings, maturity values, and annual percentage yields. Understanding CD calculations helps you maximize your savings returns and choose the best deposit terms for your financial goals.

howTo.title: How to Use the CD Calculator

steps.title: Initial Deposit
steps.description: Enter the principal amount you plan to invest in the Certificate of Deposit.

steps.title: Interest Rate
steps.description: Input the annual percentage yield (APY) or interest rate offered by the bank.

steps.title: Term Length
steps.description: Select the CD term length from 3 months to 5 years or enter a custom term period.

steps.title: Compounding Frequency
steps.description: Choose how often interest compounds: daily, monthly, quarterly, or annually.

steps.title: Additional Deposits
steps.description: For add-on CDs, specify any additional deposits you plan to make during the term.

steps.title: Review Results
steps.description: Analyze total interest earned, final balance, and effective annual yield for your CD investment.

faq.q: What's the difference between CD interest rate and APY?
faq.a: The interest rate is the nominal rate, while APY (Annual Percentage Yield) includes the effect of compounding. APY gives you the true annual return and is the better metric for comparing CDs from different institutions.

faq.q: How often do CDs compound interest?
faq.a: Most CDs compound interest daily or monthly, though some compound quarterly or annually. More frequent compounding results in slightly higher returns. Always check the compounding frequency when comparing CD offers.

faq.q: What happens if I withdraw money early from a CD?
faq.a: Early withdrawal typically results in penalties, often 3-12 months of interest depending on the CD term. Some banks may also charge principal if you haven't earned enough interest. Always understand penalty terms before investing.

faq.q: Are CDs better than high-yield savings accounts?
faq.a: CDs typically offer higher rates but lock up your money for a fixed term. High-yield savings accounts offer more liquidity but usually lower rates. Choose based on your liquidity needs and rate preferences.
